constraints.snippet: Maximum active-power ramp ≤ 20 MW/min under normal operation; settings are reviewed and demonstrated; energization inrush and steps must respect RVC limits.
constraints.source_section: Southern Company — Table 1 (Load Management (size, smoothing, and ramping))
constraints.notes: Applies to transmission-connected large loads (≥50 MW at >40 kV, or smaller facilities designated by SCT); also summarized in Section 2.1 (p. 3).

constraints.snippet: Customer submits a Load Ramp Schedule describing step magnitudes, cadence, reconnect/dropout thresholds, and delays; AEP checks steps/ramps against flicker and RVC planning limits and may require mitigation.
constraints.source_section: AEP — Table 1 (Load Management (size, smoothing, and ramping))
constraints.notes: Case-by-case review; no uniform numeric step or ramp cap published.

constraints.snippet: Flicker/RVC must meet IEEE 1453; harmonic expectations are reviewed for modern electronic equipment.
Customer should provide site-specific data (load type and transfers) and a staged reconnection plan.
constraints.source_section: Dominion — Table 1 (Load Management (size, smoothing, and ramping))
constraints.notes: Applies to loads ≥50 MW or designated <50 MW facilities.

constraints.snippet: Instantaneous voltage fluctuation at the POI ≤ 3%.
constraints.notes: POI voltage limit; needs grid impedance, not checkable from load profile alone.

constraints.snippet: Behavior governed by the commissioning plan, set by the transmission service provider based on study limits; no explicit step/ramp is defined.
constraints.source_section: ERCOT — Table 1 (Load Management (size, smoothing, and ramping))
constraints.notes: Applies to ≥75 MW at a single site; visibility threshold ≥25 MW at a common substation.

constraints.snippet: Harmonics must meet IEEE 519; Ameren may install POI meter; customer must mitigate if limits are violated. Flicker/RVC assessed to IEEE 1453; e.g., 2.0% critical-bus dip is marginal and may require mitigation. PF outside 95% lag–95% lead requires customer-side correction.

Enforces Electric Rule 2 at the POI; total voltage THD ≤ 5% and the customer funds mitigation. Phase balance: difference between any two phases at peak load should not exceed ~10%. CAISO PF band is 97% lag–99% lead.

Comply with SCT’s PQ policy; stricter limits may be imposed from study results. Provide expected harmonic spectrum to the 50th order; SCT may require mitigation and can temporarily reduce or disconnect the load.
For electronic loads, operate in constant-current mode during disturbances and avoid constant-power mode; no steady-state step/ramp defined.
constraints.source_section: SPP — Table 1 (Load Management (size, smoothing, and ramping))
constraints.notes: Applies to high-impact large loads (>10 MW at 69 kV or >50 MW at higher voltages).

constraints.snippet: SPP has published a time-voltage curve (0.90–1.10 pu continuous, with short-duration tolerances down to ~0.50 pu for ~0.15 s) and transient overvoltage withstand aligned with IEEE 2800.

ERCOT’s proposed large-load VRT requires continuous operation between 0.90–1.10 pu, with staged ride-through outside that range based on the ITIC curve, global experience, and existing IBR requirements (see Section 3).
Remain connected through several automatic reclosing shots (50-70 ms); recommend undervoltage pickup ≤85% with short timers to avoid nuisance transfers.
Example withstand: continuous 58.8–61.2 Hz; extended tolerance for 299 s outside that band; trip permissible above ~61.8 Hz or below ~57.0 Hz.
UFLS stages near 59.3, 59.0, and 58.7 Hz (~10% each).
Proposed target (Area B): recover to ≥90% of pre-disturbance consumption within 1 second once VPOI ≥ 0.9pu; if disconnected (Area C), restoration is staggered across multiple large loads.
Customer provides staged reconnection and ramp plans (thresholds, delays, block sizes, ramps); AEP coordinates to avoid secondary dips and RVCs.

No utility-wide numeric minimum level/max time; restoration follows approved operating procedures and validated ramp limits; curtailment capability and ramp-rate performance are checked before “Full Readiness.”

After any separation, the operator notifies the Control Center and obtains permission before reconnecting; unattended remote restoration requires verification that the circuit is energized from a PG&E-approved source.

Each POI includes remotely operable disconnect devices able to interrupt fault current and isolate the load; the study scope includes steady-state, stability, short-circuit, and Subsynchronous Oscillation (SSO) considerations.
Operational telemetry to ERCOT at ≤10-s scan rate with condition detection; continuous breaker/switch state is needed. Fully redundant ICCP links with automatic failover.
Permanent POI PQ meters; time-aligned, high-resolution logging with ≥ 90-day retention.
For Continental Europe, this means a continuous operating window of 0.90–1.05 pu and a sustained band of 1.05–1.10 pu for 20–60 minutes, as set by the transmission operator.
